The *Padumadhārikattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text located within the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Buddhist canon, bearing the designation Tha Ap 522 [SuttaCentral]. Beloging to the biographical and karmic poetry preserved in the late canonical strata, the text recounts the past deeds and spiritual attainment of the elder (thera) Padumadhārika [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the poem across five modern languages [SuttaCentral].
No external cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are recorded with significant scores [DharmaNexus]. However, computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 120 matching passages across 44 different Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Passages from the poem are shared with or cited in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (both parts 1 and 2), with close matches occurring across segments §1.1–4.1 [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, the text exhibits strong formulaic and thematic overlap with multiple other verses in the *Therāpadāna*, sharing substantial runs of verses with the *Padumapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 349), *Padumakūṭāgāriyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 397), *Sālamaṇḍapiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 492), *Kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 519), and *Ambāṭakiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 448) [DharmaNexus].
